name: Low-grade astrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of diffuse astrocytic tumor with low cellularity and mild nuclear atypia
MRI showing non-enhancing or minimally enhancing infiltrative lesion in the cerebral hemispheres
Presence of IDH1 or IDH2 mutation without 1p/19q co-deletion
Neurological symptoms consistent with a slowly progressive focal brain lesion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus supportive imaging and molecular findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing is critical to distinguish from other gliomas and guide prognosis.

searchTerms: seizures starting in one brain area
head pain due to increased fluid in brain

common.symptomName: Motor weakness localized to tumor site

searchTerms: loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting due to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from increased brain pressure
vomiting due to raised intracranial pressure
headache with nausea caused by brain swelling
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
imaging: MRI: T2 hyperintense, non-enhancing or faintly enhancing lesion
Lack of significant mass effect or edema compared to high-grade gliomas
genetic: ATRX loss and TP53 mutation common
other: Histopathology: low cellularity, mild nuclear atypia, absence of necrosis and microvascular proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of necrosis and microvascular proliferation on histology
Different molecular profile (IDH mutation with 1p/19q co-deletion)

redFlags: New onset of severe headaches with vomiting
Sudden onset of seizures or status epilepticus
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
Ostrom QT et al. CBTRUS Statistical Report: Primary Brain and Other Central Nervous System Tumors Diagnosed in the United States, 2014-2018
Wesseling P, Capper D. WHO 2016 Classification of gliomas. Neuropathol Appl Neurobiol. 2018
